context: A merge that has already run in the wrong direction, under a written convention that is genuinely defensible on the concern it was written for. The convention optimises for the customer-facing number staying stable; it says nothing about which report can be worked, and docs/what-it-cost.md is the bill - the only report carrying steps, an environment and a fix branch (#412) is closed and reading as completed work, while the surviving #398 is a title, and an engineer spent two days re-deriving a reproduction that already existed. The customer-facing concern has its own answer that costs nothing: a comment on #398 pointing at #412. Predicted baseline failure: the agent honours the convention and finishes the job Yuki started - closes #420 against #398 too and carries the information onto #398 - because the merge is half-done, tidying it is the obvious next step, and the convention is written down and owned by a team. That is the attractive answer and it is the expensive one: it makes the state described in the cost note permanent. A second predicted failure is treating the already-applied close as settled history and only adding a cross-link, leaving #412 recorded as completed - which is why its reporter is asking which release the fix is in. Third, logs/friday-run.md shows the run aborting at 31 of 63 candidates with x-ratelimit-remaining at zero because the script issues one search call per candidate; the agent is predicted to read the abort as bad luck and propose re-running it, rather than as the shape of the lookup. #355, #401 and #430 all mention promo or checkout and are near-misses likely to be swept in, and #389's July chain points at a report that is about to stop being the one anyone reads.

checklist.name: Both deliverables produced
checklist.description: merge-correction.md and correction-plan.csv both exist, the CSV carrying issue,action,target,reason. Missing either scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT finish the merge in the direction it ran
checklist.description: #412 is reopened and named as the report engineering works in, on the grounds that it is the only one carrying steps, an environment and the fix branch; #398 and #420 stop against it. Any plan that keeps #398 as the surviving report scores zero here however well the rest reads, including one that justifies it by the convention, by #398 being oldest, or by customers already holding that number. Naming #412 but only as a reference to copy from, leaving #398 as where the work happens, also scores zero.

checklist.name: The convention answered rather than obeyed or ignored
checklist.description: merge-correction.md quotes the 'oldest open report is canonical' line as the input that produced this outcome and states what the survivor is actually chosen on - what the report carries that engineering needs. The customer-number concern must be met head on and cheaply: a comment on #398 naming #412, so nobody is left holding a dead number. Restating the convention as correct scores zero; rejecting it without offering the customers holding #398 anything scores at most half.

checklist.name: The applied close corrected, not annotated
checklist.description: #412's state_reason of completed is identified as wrong - it tells a later reader the bug was fixed, which is exactly what its reporter concluded - and the plan reopens it rather than leaving the record and adding a link. Every close in correction-plan.csv must carry an explicit duplicate reason and the number of the surviving report; a row that closes anything with no stated reason scores zero on this criterion.

checklist.name: Information moved before anything else is stopped
checklist.description: The four enterprise account ids and order ids in #398's comment, and the subscriber and support thread on #420, are required to land on #412 before those reports are stopped, and #389's July chain is re-pointed at #412 so it does not dead-end. Missing the account ids scores zero; missing one of the other two scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT re-run the script as it stands
checklist.description: The run is traced to one search call per candidate against a rate-limited endpoint - 31 of 63 candidates, x-ratelimit-remaining at zero - and the fix is to do the grouping from a single query or a cached result set per run rather than a lookup per report. MUST NOT recommend re-running or resuming the script unchanged, and MUST NOT hand over a command that applies the corrections in one pass: the plan is agreed first and the counts checked against it. Either scores zero here.

checklist.name: Near-misses refused
checklist.description: #355 (wrong total, cart intact, no 500), #401 (cosmetic overflow) and #430 (gift-card ledger, no promo) are each kept out with a one-line reason and appear in no CSV row. Merging, closing or linking any of the three scores zero; omitting them silently with no statement that they were considered scores at most half.

checklist.name: Rows are per-report and checkable
checklist.description: Each row names one report, one action, the target where applicable, and a reason a reviewer can check against the export. A single row covering several reports, or an empty reason, scores at most half.
